title: Genius: The Life And Science Of Richard Feynman

questions.q: How did Feynman's father help him grasp the size of a dinosaur?
a: He compared it to the boy's bedroom window
He showed him photographs from a textbook
He took him to a natural history museum
He drew the skeleton on paper
questions.why: The first lesson says Melville made numbers concrete by tying them to something Richard could picture.

questions.q: Why did Melville teach his son bird names in other languages?
a: To show that naming a bird is not the same as understanding it
To prepare him for a career abroad
To make him memorize more vocabulary
To test whether he could spell them
questions.why: The first lesson says real knowledge came from watching what a bird does, not from its label.

questions.q: How did Feynman solve the problem of the hat falling into the river?
a: He imagined himself as the hat
He wrote out the velocity formulas
He estimated from the water speed
He recalled a similar textbook problem
questions.why: The second lesson says he saw instantly that the numbers were irrelevant and the answer was 45 minutes.

questions.q: What does the summary claim about IQ and EQ?
a: EQ matters as much as IQ, if not more
IQ predicts success far better than EQ
EQ can safely be ignored by scientists
The two have no connection to each other
questions.why: The second lesson says Feynman's empathy, putting himself in the shoes of atoms, powered his problem-solving.

questions.q: What lesson does the summary draw from Feynman's weak subjects?
a: Know your weaknesses and invest in your strengths
Never admit to anyone what you are bad at
Force yourself to master every subject equally
Choose a career that avoids all writing
questions.why: The third lesson says fighting uphill battles wastes time you could spend expanding what you are great at.
